corrections.old: The HJB equation $0=\min_{|u|\le1}[1+V'(x)u]=1-|V'(x)|$ holds wherever $V$ is differentiable; at kinks it holds in a weak sense, through inequalities for smooth test functions touching $V$ from above or below. In this viscosity sense the equation (and the variational inequalities of reachability) has a unique solution, the value function; the modules use it as an interface to grid-based solvers.
corrections.new: Where $V$ is differentiable, the HJB equation is $0=\min_{|u|\le1}[1+V'(x)u]=1-|V'(x)|$. For the viscosity formulation use $|V'(x)|-1=0$ on $(-1,1)$ with boundary values $V(-1)=V(1)=0$: the sign matters in the inequalities for smooth test functions touching $V$ from above or below. At the kink, a test function touching from above has slope in $[-1,1]$, so the subsolution inequality $|\varphi'|-1\le0$ holds; no smooth test function touches from below there. This boundary-value problem has the unique continuous viscosity solution $1-|x|$. More general HJB and reachability equations need their own comparison-principle and boundary assumptions for uniqueness; the modules use these results as an interface to grid-based solvers.
corrections.reason: Multiplying a classical PDE by -1 preserves classical zeros but reverses viscosity inequalities; uniqueness also needs a specified boundary-value problem.
